standard_prerequisites.use: Reduce the property to the chart morphisms $U \to W$ and $V \to W$.

core_obligations: Build the chart tower $W \to Z$, $V \to W \times_Z Y$, $U \to V \times_Y X$ with all arrows surjective \'etale (proof lines 892-897).

Lift: by the sheaf-surjection hypothesis there is an fppf covering $\{V_i \to V\}$ with lifts $V_i \to X$; composing with $U \to X$ surjective \'etale and base changing gives lifts into $U$ over the covering $\{V_i \times_X U \to V\}$, so $U \to V$ induces a surjection of sheaves (proof lines 897-905).

By the definitions of flat/locally finite type/locally finite presentation for algebraic-space morphisms (cited definitions), $U \to W$ has the property and it suffices to show $V \to W$ does; conclude by the scheme case (proof lines 905-911).
proof_roadmap: Lift the covering through the sheaf surjection, twice.
Reduce to schemes via the chart definitions and apply the scheme case.
difficulty_reason: The proof builds a three-level chart tower $W \to Z$, $V \to W \times_Z Y$, $U \to V \times_Y X$, uses the sheaf-surjection hypothesis to lift members of an fppf covering $\{V_i \to V\}$ into $X$ and then (through $U \to X$ surjective \'etale) into $U$, obtaining that $U \to V$ induces a surjection of sheaves; the definitions of the three properties for algebraic-space morphisms via charts reduce everything to the scheme case.
